phrase.text: Spaces, tabs and line breaks only separate pieces: indentation does not change the meaning and a line break does not end a statement.

runs.text: Spaces, tabs and line breaks only separate pieces: indentation does not change the meaning and a line break does not end a statement.
Between two words of a program there may be one space, many, or a line break: it makes no difference to the engine.
(the spaces at the start of a line) has no meaning either. It is used so that people can see what is inside what, but the engine follows the opening and closing words, such as

runs.text: This program has careless indentation and extra spaces; even so it runs exactly like a well-written one:

blocks.title: Careless indentation

runs.text: replace the semicolon. If you forget the
, the engine points it out even if the next statement starts on another line. Multi-word reserved words, such as
, cannot be split across two lines either.

Ask the class to write the same program with two different indentations and run it: the result does not change. Then explain why indentation is still essential for reading it. It is a good way of separating "what the machine understands" from "what a person needs".

points.text: Spaces, tabs and line breaks only separate pieces.
Indentation means nothing to the engine, but a lot to people.
A line break does not replace the semicolon.
